messages:
Anna (CEO): Thanks for joining the post-all-hands follow-up. Wanted a short thread where we capture sharp questions about our mission and how we should talk about differentiation vs. big cloud and model-hosting vendors. Keep replies short so leadership can batch responses.
Sam (Head of Sales): Customers keep asking: is Redwood a performance play or a compliance play? Need one line for calls.
Jai (VP Product): One line we can use: 'Redwood is the inference runtime — we turn models into predictable, economical services with enterprise-grade controls.' Does that land?
Sam (Head of Sales): Better. Add something about consistent API across environments.
Emily (Head of Research): From a research angle, customers also ask whether we prefer partnering with open models or licensing big closed models. Quick position?
Jai (VP Product): Default: we curate open and vetted models plus support vendor-licensed variants where customers demand them. We prioritize serving predictability over model exclusivity.
Maya: Ops ask: how aggressive should we be about publishing benchmark numbers vs. caution about reproducibility?
Anna (CEO): Publish standard, reproducible benchmarks (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, throughput) and add a reproducibility appendix. Call out caveats prominently. Transparency is a differentiator.
Sam (Head of Sales): Competitors question: how do we answer "why not run on managed cloud endpoints?" short script please.
Jai (VP Product): Script: 'Managed endpoints give you models; Redwood gives you predictable production behavior: lower tail latency, cost controls, rollout safety, and predictable economics across deployments.'
Emily (Head of Research): Follow-up: will we invest more in quantization and kernel work this year or more in rollout/observability? What's the product priority?
Anna (CEO): Priority split: infra/runtime (quantization, kernels) remains strategic long-term; this quarter we bias a bit more to rollout/observability because it unlocks larger adoption and immediate ARR.
Maya: Hiring practical question: should CV/LLM infra hires be placed in Eng-Runtime or Eng-ML?
Jai (VP Product): Mix: core kernel work -> Eng-Runtime; model/quant tuning and evals -> Eng-ML. We'll publish a short org guide for new hires.
DeployBot: deploy-notify: docs-site redeploy succeeded (ci 1987)
Sam (Head of Sales): One last ask: can leadership give a single metric to rally around this quarter (north star)?
Anna (CEO): North star: active paid deployments (customers with >1 route in production) and 95th-percentile latency SLA attainment. Short, measurable, and ties GTM and product.
Jai (VP Product): I'll draft a 1-page FAQ and the two short scripts (sales + cloud comparison) and post here tomorrow.
Anna (CEO): Great. If anyone has follow-ups drop them now; we'll fold answers into the public roadmap doc and the next all-hands notes. :thumbsup:
